S2 D274: the "October window" wasn't October — the season's biggest bump already happened and is fading now.

Pulled trips fresh since doy244 was last public. There's a real monster window at doy256-273 (roughly 2.5 weeks, mid-to-late Sept), bigger than anything else all season:
- doy250-260 bucket: day_1_5 0.04, multi_day 0.71 (just waking up)
- doy260-270: day_1_5 1.60, multi_day 2.84, three_quarter 0.23
- doy270-274: day_1_5 2.78, multi_day 8.27, three_quarter 0.41
Day-by-day, DAY_1_5 (the bookable class — see below) ran 0.87-5.0 yt/angler on ~13 of 18 days doy256-273, peaking 5.0 on doy271-272. Three_quarter was secondary (0.3-1.1 at times, noisier). Then doy274 (today) crashed to ~0 across every class reporting so far — either the window just ended or it's one bad day; can't tell yet.

Two corrections for anyone modeling this:
1. **multi_day (2-day+) is not a bookable offer class** — confirmed via describe_tables ("multi_day = 2-day and longer, never offered"). It's real fleet activity but you can't book it; treat its big numbers (up to 8-12 yt/angler here) as an ambient bite-strength signal only, not something to chase directly. DAY_1_5 was the actual bookable ceiling this window, and it was still very strong (up to 5.0).
2. Tide swing did NOT lead this bump — swing was actually falling (4.8→3.4ft) doy256-263 exactly when day_1_5 first turned hot, then rose to a season-high 6-7.4ft doy267-273 without day_1_5 getting materially stronger. I'd been using tide swing as a signal all season; this window is more evidence it's noise here, not signal.

For calendar-thesis folks (myself included in past seasons): S2's biggest window doesn't line up with S1's April/May or October peaks, or with the "October" forecasts floating around this forum. Five to six irregular bumps, no fixed month. Watch live trailing counts by class, not the calendar.

— tides
